content:
Hong Kong Comics and Animation Festival 2026 opened today (the 24th), an event that has long been a summer tradition for Hong Kong residents. As early as 9 a.m., citizens were waiting outside the Convention and Exhibition Centre to enter. The first-prize winners were admitted at 10 a.m., continuing the tradition of the "anti-intellectual turn." Some exhibition areas quickly became crowded shortly after opening.

Mr. Yip, who was at the front of the line, headed straight to the Sanrio booth upon entry to purchase Hong Kong-exclusive Egypt-themed "Cinnamoroll" and "Pompompurin" plush toys, with a long queue forming at the booth.

Mr. Yip, who has attended the event in previous years, registered for the lottery for the first time this year and struck it lucky on his first attempt, winning "first prize." He performed the "anti-intellectual turn" first thing after entering, saying he wanted to carry on the tradition of the Comics Festival. He later went to the Sanrio booth to buy Hong Kong-exclusive Egypt-themed "Cinnamoroll" and "Pompompurin" plush toys, and plans to spend around HK$1,000 today on his favourite items.

Mr. Hung, also part of the first-prize group, said he has been attending since the age of six and it has become a habit for over a decade. He laughed and said this year he could witness the "anti-intellectual turn" up close. He mentioned that over the past ten-plus years he has witnessed the evolution of the comics and animation exhibition, including the changes in the doujin (fan-made) exhibitor booths. He said that as a child he might not have visited them, but as he became exposed to more games, he realised that Hong Kong's doujin creations have been developing in tandem, and in recent years have even formed their own dedicated zone, allowing different people to each pursue the works they want. He said he would first visit Hall 1 to buy models, figures and the like, then head to the Doujin Festival venue.

Although he won the first-prize lottery, Mr. Hung believes the lottery system has its pros and cons: "They might have arrived very early, maybe as early as 6 a.m. to queue, but they still end up behind position 300, and they might not be able to buy what they want."

At 10 a.m. this morning, first-prize winners were able to head to their desired booths first to purchase their favourite items, with the longest queues seen at Hong Kong brands Hot Toys, Bandai's model division, and Sanrio. According to records, the Comics Festival officially introduced a real-name registration lottery system in 2018 to prevent overnight queuing and scalping, with 500 slots initially offered, later reduced to 300 in recent years.

Beyblade has returned to the exhibition after more than a decade, with the distributor setting up Beyblade arenas at the booth for players to battle.

This year's Comics Festival is the largest in history, with over 200 exhibitors participating and nearly 700 manga artists and designers taking part. The exhibition venue has also been expanded to Hall 5, used as CosParadise, with the fees for photographer and cosplayer passes increased by 10 percent, allowing them to enter through dedicated access. However, despite the expanded venue, this year's arrangements require visitors holding the HK$50 full-price ticket to first enter the first-floor exhibition hall in order, before proceeding to the third-floor Doujin Festival and the fifth-floor CosParadise, and entry is limited to one time only. After the first round of admission this morning, the crowd remained concentrated on the first floor, and it was not until around noon that crowds gradually dispersed to other exhibition areas on other floors.
